clue.text: Clue: Dash by, short of time

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: to scoot is to dash off
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint: someone dashing past while short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T of time from the dash-word before BY is added. 'Not a Scooby' is British rhyming slang (Scooby-Doo = clue) for having no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang Scooby-Doo stands for clue, shortened in everyday speech to just the first word.

clue.text: Comedian is let down

blocks.note: first meaning: a performer of solo comedy before an audience
second meaning: to stand someone up is to fail to keep a date with them

explanation.surface: A comic who has been disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up is a solo comic, and someone stood up has been jilted by a no-show date.

clue.text: Repeated denial about being cut by top of incandescent bulb

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the repeated denial is read backwards
in a down clue the top is the start, so only the first letter is taken
to be cut by something is to have it go into you, so one letter is inserted

blocks.note: saying no twice
its first letter

explanation.surface: A double refusal about cutting into a glowing light bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incandescent bulb' suggests a lamp; the bulb is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is the edible bulb of an allium plant, so bulb is a category it belongs to.

clue.text: Fern Britton's head stand when half-cut

indicators.note: the head is the leading part, so only the first letter is used
cutting a word in half keeps one half of its letters, here the back half

blocks.note: its first letter
a rack is a stand for holding things
its second half

explanation.surface: TV presenter Fern Britton's head stand, attempted after a drink or two.
explanation.walkthrough: Fern Britton is a British TV presenter, so 'Fern' seems part of her name; it is the definition. Half-cut is British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracken is a large, coarse fern that covers moorland and hillsides.

clue.text: Turner masterpiece mostly displayed in Greek city

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: 'The Best' is a signature song of the singer Tina Turner

explanation.surface: A painting by J. M. W. Turner being exhibited in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the painter Turner, but it is Tina Turner and her hit song 'The Best', minus its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was an important ancient city-state in Boeotia, and a modern town of that name still stands there.

clue.text: Hooked up, I see, with friend

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: ah is what you say when you understand
mate is informal for a friend

explanation.surface: Someone realising they have got together with a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooked up' reads as a phrase about pairing off; up is the reversal signal and hooked alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamate is a technical adjective for hook-shaped, as in the hamate bone of the wrist.

clue.text: Initially, England and Australia support cricketers providing home for rescued dogs

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so just the first letters are taken
in a down entry a support goes underneath, so these letters come after

blocks.note: batters are players in a cricket team
the first letter of each country

explanation.surface: Both Test nations backing their cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs and Cats Home in south London is Britain's best-known animal rescue centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a London district whose famous refuge for stray and abandoned animals is known by the area's name.

clue.text: Expert supports outrageous risk in competition

indicators.note: something outrageous is wild and out of order, so these letters are rearranged
in a down entry a support is underneath, so this piece comes last

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A professional backing someone taking a wild chance in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski race is a downhill or slalom contest on snow, so it is a sporting competition.

clue.text: Description of flower power?

blocks.note: surface reading: the 1960s hippy slogan about peace and blossoms
setter's reading: a flower is something that flows, a river, so its power is energy generated from running water

explanation.walkthrough: Flower is crossword code for river (it flows); the answer describes power drawn from water.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity produced by turbines driven by flowing water is the kind of power a river supplies.

clue.text: Nation formalises borders

indicators.note: to border something is to surround it, so the outer word encloses the answer

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A country making something official, set around its frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country of West Africa, so it is a nation.

clue.text: Time my car's scrapped; it's unbalanced

indicators.note: a scrapped car is broken up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: An owner deciding to send a lopsided old car to the scrapyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something asymmetric lacks matching halves, so it is lopsided or out of balance.

clue.text: Martial arts experts visiting Greek port

indicators.note: visitors go inside a place, so these letters sit inside the other piece

blocks.note: GK is an abbreviation for Greek
a dan is a black-belt grade in judo or karate, or one who holds it

explanation.surface: Kung-fu masters calling in at a harbour in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek port' reads as one phrase, but Greek is wordplay and port alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is the major Baltic seaport of Poland, on the Gulf of Gdansk.

clue.text: People, not us, run to the front and are close to ecstasy in Scottish seaside resort

indicators.note: this letter leaves its place and is moved to the head of the word
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
other people, as opposed to ourselves
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
its last letter

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers rushing ahead to an ecstatic arrival at a Scottish beach town.
explanation.walkthrough: The R inside the word for other people moves to the front, then A for are and the end of ecstasy follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rothesay is the chief town on the Isle of Bute, a traditional Clyde holiday resort.

clue.text: What often happened after 72 holes is not clearly defined

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: golf's Open championship is decided over 72 holes
second meaning: without fixed limits or a set conclusion

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer as two words: the Open (golf's major championship, played over four 18-hole rounds) ended.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-ended question or arrangement has no fixed limit, so it is vague rather than precisely bounded.

clue.text: In Stirling, result of trial of drunk patron dumping a kiln

indicators.note: dumping something gets rid of it, so the letter named is removed
a drunk person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a kiln is an oven for firing pottery

explanation.surface: A drunken customer ditching a kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirling is a Scottish town; Scots law has a third verdict besides guilty and not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Not proven is a verdict available to Scottish courts, so it is a possible outcome of a trial in Scotland.

clue.text: Terrible lie about introduction to Scarborough Fair?

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the single letter
an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
its first letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful falsehood about the folk song 'Scarborough Fair'.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Fair Isle is a Shetland island, so Fair can precede the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is one of the Shetland islands, famous for its knitwear, so Fair can stand for one particular island.

clue.text: Takes in sustenance from nipples, first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: teats are nipples, especially on animals

explanation.surface: A suckling animal feeding from its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to take food into the body, i.e. to take in nourishment.

clue.text: Tailor almost never cut shroud

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to tailor is to alter and refit, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A tailor who very nearly never trims a burial shroud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Envelop and shroud are verbs meaning to wrap up or cover completely.

clue.text: Every individual getting ratted around centre of Leeds gets complete transformation

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the informer's word encloses the other piece
the centre is the middle, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing on someone, as is to rat
each means every one taken individually
the middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: Everyone being informed on in Leeds, and the city utterly changed as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'sing' is slang for informing to the police, so ratted (informed) gives the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea change, from Shakespeare's The Tempest, is a profound alteration or total transformation.

clue.text: Cleavage, extremely large, seen in China?

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, so the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: a crack is a split or cleavage
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cleavage and plunging necklines spotted in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C disguises china (porcelain) as the country; the question mark flags the definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackle is the network of fine cracks deliberately produced in the glaze of porcelain.

clue.text: Good babies scintillate

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a litter is a group of babies born together to an animal

explanation.surface: Well-behaved infants shining brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to sparkle with flashes of light, just as to scintillate is.

clue.text: Macho Russian guards sing together

indicators.note: to guard is to keep something enclosed, so the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Tough Russian security men singing in unison.
explanation.definitionFit: To chorus is a verb meaning to say or sing something simultaneously as a group.

clue.text: Paramours left scratched — getting passionate went too far

indicators.note: a scratched runner is withdrawn, so this letter is removed

blocks.note: a paramour is an illicit lover
L is the abbreviation for left
hot can mean passionate or ardent

explanation.surface: Illicit lovers, scratched in a row, letting things become too heated.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go past a target, so the past tense means went beyond the intended point.

clue.text: Former car capital of America

blocks.note: first meaning: a British car marque, no longer made
second meaning: the state capital of Texas, in the USA

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of America' suggests Washington, but any state capital in the USA qualifies. Austin was a British car maker, later part of British Leyland.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is both a defunct British motor brand and the city that is the seat of Texas state government.

clue.text: Clever vehicles reversed

indicators.note: the word is backed up and spelt from end to start

blocks.note: trams are vehicles running on rails

explanation.surface: Skilful drivers backing their cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and clever are adjectives both meaning quick-witted or intelligent.

clue.text: Self-satisfied know-all oddly calmed by decision to throw out Thailand and Cambodia

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, so the first, third and fifth letters are kept
throwing something out discards it, so this letter is removed

blocks.note: letters one, three and five
a verdict is a decision, as from a jury
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
K is the international vehicle code for Cambodia

explanation.surface: A smug expert soothed by a ruling expelling two Asian nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Thailand's T is thrown out of the decision and Cambodia's K is added at the end. A clever dick is British slang for a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever dick is British informal for a person who smugly displays knowledge, i.e. a smart alec.

clue.text: I'm opposed to granny dating, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the middle letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
the two central letters

explanation.surface: Someone disapproving of their grandmother going on dates.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 'I'm', the definition gives the sentence 'I'm anti', the speaker's objection.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti works as a preposition or adjective meaning against or hostile to something.

clue.text: Amusing wordplay is hard to beat

blocks.note: a pun is a joke built on words
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A remark that a clever play on words is difficult to better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to beat' looks like one phrase meaning unbeatable; split it, hard gives a letter and beat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone as a penalty is to discipline them, which is a synonym-level match for inflicting punishment.

clue.text: Retch horribly around old Harry

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so these letters are scrambled
around means encircling, so the scrambled letters surround the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone gagging badly near an old man called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name, but here it is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector and to harry both mean to bully or badger someone persistently.
